AUTH-API-001.scenario: Check that the login API refuses a request with an empty body
AUTH-API-001.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with an empty JSON body {}.
Read the response status, error code and field errors.
AUTH-API-001.expected: The API answers 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR and field errors for both email and password.

AUTH-API-002.scenario: Check that the login API refuses a request when email or password is missing
AUTH-API-002.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with a password and location but no email.
Read the response status, error code and field errors.
Repeat with an email and location but no password.
AUTH-API-002.test_data: Variant 1 (no email): {"password": "Wrong@Pass1", "clientGeo": {"latitude": <configured latitude>, "longitude": <configured longitude>, "timezone": "Asia/Calcutta"}}. Variant 2 (no password): {"email": "qa.nobody.7x@example.com", "clientGeo": {"latitude": <configured latitude>, "longitude": <configured longitude>, "timezone": "Asia/Calcutta"}}
AUTH-API-002.expected: Each request gets 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR and a field error naming the missing field (email or password).

AUTH-API-003.scenario: Check that the login API refuses email addresses in an invalid format
AUTH-API-003.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with a badly formatted email, a password and a valid location.
Read the response status, error code and field errors.
Repeat for each email in the test data.
AUTH-API-003.test_data: Email values: "abc", "abc@", "a b@x.com", "@x.com"; password "Wrong@Pass1"; valid clientGeo.
AUTH-API-003.expected: Each request gets 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR and a field error for email.

AUTH-API-004.scenario: Check that the login API refuses a sign-in that has no location (clientGeo)
AUTH-API-004.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with an email and password but without the clientGeo block.
Read the response status, error code and message.
AUTH-API-004.expected: The API answers 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR and a message containing "Location access is required".

AUTH-API-005.scenario: Check that the login API refuses an email that has no account
AUTH-API-005.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with an unknown email, any password and a valid location.
Read the response status, error code and message.
AUTH-API-005.expected: The API answers 401 with code UNAUTHORIZED and the message "Invalid email or password."

AUTH-API-006.scenario: Verify that a wrong password for a real account gets exactly the same answer as an unknown email
AUTH-API-006.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed. The admin email and password are configured for the test run. Only one wrong-password attempt is made on the real account per run.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with the real admin email, a wrong password and a valid location.
Note the response status, error code and message.
Send the same request with an unknown email (qa.nobody.7x@example.com).
Compare the two responses.
AUTH-API-006.test_data: Request 1: real admin email + password "Wrong@Pass1". Request 2: "qa.nobody.7x@example.com" + "Wrong@Pass1". Both with valid clientGeo.
AUTH-API-006.expected: Both responses have the same status, error code and message, and the wrong-password response is 401. An attacker cannot tell which emails have accounts.

AUTH-API-007.scenario: Check that the login API handles a broken JSON body cleanly
AUTH-API-007.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with Content-Type application/json and a cut-off JSON body.
Read the response status and error code.
AUTH-API-007.expected: The API answers 400 with code MALFORMED_REQUEST, not a 500 server error.

AUTH-API-008.scenario: Check that the login API refuses impossible location values
AUTH-API-008.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with an unknown email, a password and an invalid clientGeo block.
Read the response status.
Repeat for each location variant in the test data.
AUTH-API-008.expected: Each request is refused with a 4xx status - never a success (2xx) and never a server error (5xx).

AUTH-API-009.scenario: Verify that SQL injection text in the email and password never signs in or causes a database error
AUTH-API-009.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with the same SQL injection text as both email and password, plus a valid location.
Read the response status and body.
Repeat for each payload in the test data.
AUTH-API-009.test_data: Payloads (used as both email and password): ' OR '1'='1 | admin'-- | " OR ""=" | ') OR ('1'='1 | 1 OR 1=1
AUTH-API-009.expected: Each request answers 400, 401 or 403 (a firewall block is fine). No request signs in (2xx) or causes a server error (5xx), and the body contains no "sql" or "syntax" error text.

AUTH-API-010.scenario: Check that the login API refuses a very long (10,000-character) email or password cleanly
AUTH-API-010.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with a 10,000-character email (plus @example.com), a normal password and a valid location.
Read the response status.
Send another request with the normal unknown email and a password of about 10,000 characters.
AUTH-API-010.test_data: Variant 1: email = 10,000 x "a" + "@example.com". Variant 2: email "qa.nobody.7x@example.com", password = "A@1" + 10,000 x "a".
AUTH-API-010.expected: Both requests are refused with a 4xx status (for example 400, 401 or 413), never a 2xx or 5xx.

AUTH-API-011.scenario: Check that the login API refuses a form-encoded body cleanly
AUTH-API-011.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded and a form body.
Read the response status.
AUTH-API-011.expected: The API refuses the request with a 4xx status (for example 400 or 415), not a 500 server error.

AUTH-API-012.scenario: Check that the login endpoint accepts only POST and refuses other HTTP methods
AUTH-API-012.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a GET request to /api/v1/auth/login without a token.
Read the response status.
Repeat with PUT and DELETE.
AUTH-API-012.test_data: Methods: GET, PUT, DELETE (no body, no token)
AUTH-API-012.expected: Each method is refused with 405, 401, 403 or 404 (401 is accepted because the auth check runs first). None returns a 2xx success.

AUTH-API-013.scenario: Verify that the correct password alone gives no session token and asks for an OTP
AUTH-API-013.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed. The admin email and password are configured for the test run. Note: this sends one OTP email to the admin mailbox.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with the real admin email, the correct password and a valid location.
Check the response status.
Check the response data for otpRequired, a challenge reference and the OTP destination.
Check that the response contains no access token.
AUTH-API-013.expected: The API answers 200 with otpRequired = true, a challengeReference, and a masked OTP destination (with dot characters, not the full email). No accessToken is returned.

AUTH-API-020.scenario: Check that the verify-OTP API refuses an empty request and names the missing fields
AUTH-API-020.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/verify-otp with an empty JSON body {}.
Read the response status, error code and field errors.
AUTH-API-020.expected: The API answers 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR and field errors for challengeReference and code.

AUTH-API-021.scenario: Check that verifying a code for an unknown or expired challenge tells the user to sign in again
AUTH-API-021.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/verify-otp with a made-up challenge reference and a code.
Read the response status, error code and message.
AUTH-API-021.expected: The API answers 401 with code OTP_RESTART_REQUIRED and the message "This code can no longer be used. Sign in again to get a new one."

AUTH-API-022.scenario: Check that the verify-OTP API refuses codes that are not exactly 6 digits
AUTH-API-022.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/verify-otp with a made-up challenge reference and a badly formatted code.
Read the response status.
Repeat for each code in the test data.
AUTH-API-022.expected: Each request is refused with 400 or 401 - never a success (2xx) or server error (5xx).

AUTH-API-023.scenario: Check that resending an OTP for an unknown challenge tells the user to sign in again
AUTH-API-023.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/resend-otp with a made-up challenge reference.
Read the response status and error code.
AUTH-API-023.expected: The API answers 401 with code OTP_RESTART_REQUIRED.

AUTH-API-024.scenario: Verify that repeated wrong OTP codes on one sign-in attempt are stopped within 6 tries
AUTH-API-024.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed. The admin email and password are configured for the test run. Opt-in test: runs only when RUN_LOCKOUT_TESTS=1 is set, because it can lock the account or throttle this machine's IP. Run it on its own at the end of a session. Sends one OTP email to the admin.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with the real admin email and correct password to get a challenge reference.
Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/verify-otp with that challenge reference and a wrong code.
Read the response status and error code.
Keep sending wrong codes (up to 6 in total), stopping when the API blocks further tries.
AUTH-API-024.expected: Within 6 wrong codes the API stops accepting guesses - it answers 429 (too many requests) or code OTP_RESTART_REQUIRED.

AUTH-API-030.scenario: Verify that /auth/me with a valid token returns the signed-in user and no secrets
AUTH-API-030.preconditions: The API is reachable. The admin account is set up and a valid sign-in token for the admin is available (taken from a signed-in browser session).
steps: Send a GET request to /api/v1/auth/me with the header Authorization: Bearer <valid token>.
Check the response status.
Check the response body for the user's email and for any password, OTP or secret fields.
AUTH-API-030.expected: The API answers 200, the body contains the admin's email, and there is no "password", "otp" or "secret" field.

AUTH-API-031.scenario: Verify that session and data endpoints refuse calls without a sign-in token
AUTH-API-031.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a GET request to /api/v1/auth/me without any Authorization header.
Read the response status and error code.
Repeat for each endpoint in the test data.
AUTH-API-031.expected: Every call answers 401 with code UNAUTHORIZED.

AUTH-API-032.scenario: Verify that /auth/me refuses garbage, empty or wrong-type Authorization headers
AUTH-API-032.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a GET request to /api/v1/auth/me with an invalid Authorization header.
Read the response status.
Repeat for each header value in the test data.
AUTH-API-032.test_data: Authorization values: "Bearer abc.def.ghi" (garbage), "Bearer " (empty), "Basic YWRtaW46YWRtaW4=" (Basic admin:admin), "Token x" (wrong scheme)

AUTH-API-033.scenario: Verify that a real token with one changed signature character is refused
AUTH-API-033.preconditions: The API is reachable. The admin account is set up and a valid sign-in token for the admin is available (taken from a signed-in browser session).
steps: Take a valid admin token and change the first character of its signature part (the third section).
Send a GET request to /api/v1/auth/me with Authorization: Bearer <forged token>.
Read the response status.
AUTH-API-033.test_data: Valid admin token with the first signature character replaced (A, or B if it was already A).
AUTH-API-033.expected: The API answers 401 - the server checks the token signature.

AUTH-API-034.scenario: Verify that an unsigned (alg=none) copy of a real token is refused
AUTH-API-034.preconditions: The API is reachable. The admin account is set up and a valid sign-in token for the admin is available (taken from a signed-in browser session).
steps: Build a token with header {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"}, the real token's payload, and an empty signature.
Send a GET request to /api/v1/auth/me with Authorization: Bearer <unsigned token>.
Read the response status.
AUTH-API-034.test_data: Header {"alg":"none","typ":"JWT"} + payload of the valid admin token + empty signature.
AUTH-API-034.expected: The API answers 401 - unsigned tokens are never accepted.

AUTH-API-035.scenario: Verify that changing a token's contents (a much later expiry) makes it invalid
AUTH-API-035.preconditions: The API is reachable. The admin account is set up and a valid sign-in token for the admin is available (taken from a signed-in browser session).
steps: Decode the payload of a valid admin token.
Change the expiry (exp) to about 10 years from now and re-encode the payload, keeping the original header and signature.
Send a GET request to /api/v1/auth/me with Authorization: Bearer <modified token>.
Read the response status.
AUTH-API-035.test_data: Valid admin token with exp set to now + 10 years.
AUTH-API-035.expected: The API answers 401 - a token whose contents were changed is refused.

AUTH-API-036.scenario: Verify that the sign-in token is signed, expires within an hour and carries no password or OTP
AUTH-API-036.preconditions: A valid admin sign-in token is available (taken from a signed-in browser session). No API call is made.
steps: Decode the header and payload of the admin token (for example on jwt.io).
Check the signing algorithm in the header.
Check the issued-at (iat) and expiry (exp) times and work out the token lifetime.
Check the payload for any password, passwd, OTP, code, secret or PIN value.
AUTH-API-036.expected: The algorithm is a real signing algorithm (not empty or "none"), the token has an expiry, its lifetime is more than 0 and at most 60 minutes, and no claim carries a password, OTP, code, secret or PIN as text.

AUTH-API-037.scenario: Verify that after logout the same token is refused everywhere
AUTH-API-037.preconditions: The API and web app are reachable. The admin email and password are configured for the test run. A fresh, separate sign-in is used so the shared session is not affected.
steps: Sign in to the web app as admin (email, password and OTP) and copy the access token from the browser session.
Send a GET request to /api/v1/auth/me with that token and confirm it works.
Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/logout with the same token.
Send a GET request to /api/v1/auth/me with the same token again.
Send a GET request to /api/v1/beneficiaries with the same token.
AUTH-API-037.expected: /auth/me answers 200 before logout; logout answers 200 or 204; afterwards both /auth/me and /beneficiaries answer 401 with that token.

AUTH-API-040.scenario: Check that change-password with an empty body names every missing field
AUTH-API-040.preconditions: The API is reachable. The admin account is set up and a valid sign-in token for the admin is available (taken from a signed-in browser session).
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/change-password with a valid token and an empty JSON body {}.
Read the response status, error code and field errors.
AUTH-API-040.expected: The API answers 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR and field errors for currentPassword, newPassword and confirmPassword. Nothing is changed.

AUTH-API-041.scenario: Check that a weak new password is refused and the session stays valid
AUTH-API-041.preconditions: The API is reachable. The admin account is set up and a valid sign-in token for the admin is available (taken from a signed-in browser session). A wrong current password is sent on purpose so the real password can never be changed by this test.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/change-password with a valid token, a wrong current password and a weak new password (same value in confirm).
Read the response status.
Send a GET request to /api/v1/auth/me with the same token.
Repeat for each weak password in the test data.
AUTH-API-041.test_data: currentPassword "Wrong@Cur1"; new/confirm values: "abc" (3 chars), "abcdefgh" (no capital, digit or symbol), "ABCD@1234" (no lowercase), "Abcd@12345678" (13 chars)
AUTH-API-041.expected: Each change request is refused with 400 or 422, and /auth/me still answers 200 (the session is still valid).

AUTH-API-042.scenario: Check that the server refuses a change when the new password and confirm password do not match
AUTH-API-042.preconditions: The API is reachable. The admin account is set up and a valid sign-in token for the admin is available (taken from a signed-in browser session).
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/change-password with a valid token and different values for newPassword and confirmPassword.
Read the response status.
AUTH-API-042.expected: The API refuses the request with 400 or 422.

AUTH-API-043.scenario: Check that a wrong current password is refused and the session stays valid
AUTH-API-043.preconditions: The API is reachable. The admin account is set up and a valid sign-in token for the admin is available (taken from a signed-in browser session).
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/change-password with a valid token, a wrong current password and a strong, matching new password.
Read the response status.
Send a GET request to /api/v1/auth/me with the same token.
AUTH-API-043.expected: The change is refused with 400, 401, 403 or 422 (the password is not changed), and /auth/me still answers 200.

AUTH-API-050.scenario: Verify that forgot-password for an unknown email returns the generic success message
AUTH-API-050.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/forgot-password with an email that has no account.
Read the response status and message.
AUTH-API-050.expected: The API answers 200 with a message containing "If an account exists" - it does not reveal that the account is missing.

AUTH-API-051.scenario: Verify that forgot-password gives the same answer for a real account and an unknown email
AUTH-API-051.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed. The admin email and password are configured for the test run. Note: this sends one reset email to the admin (the password is not changed).
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/forgot-password with the real admin email.
Note the response status and message.
Send the same request with an unknown email.
Compare the two responses.
AUTH-API-051.expected: Both responses have the same status and message, so nobody can find out which emails have accounts.

AUTH-API-052.scenario: Check that forgot-password refuses an empty or badly formatted email
AUTH-API-052.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/forgot-password with an invalid email.
Read the response status, error code and field errors.
Repeat for each email in the test data.
AUTH-API-052.expected: Each request answers 400 with code VALIDATION_ERROR and a field error for email.

AUTH-API-053.scenario: Verify that a made-up reset token is reported as not usable
AUTH-API-053.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/reset-password/verify with a made-up token.
Read the response status, and if it is 200, read the 'valid' value in the response data.
Repeat for each token in the test data.
AUTH-API-053.expected: Each request answers 200, 400, 403, 404 or 410. If it answers 200, the data shows valid = false. No made-up token is accepted as valid.

AUTH-API-054.scenario: Verify that a password reset with a made-up token never succeeds
AUTH-API-054.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/reset-password with a made-up token and a new password.
Read the response status.
AUTH-API-054.expected: The reset is refused with a 4xx status - not 200/204 (success) and not a 5xx server error.

AUTH-API-055.scenario: Verify that login responses carry the required security headers and are not cached
AUTH-API-055.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with an unknown email, a password and a valid location.
Look at the response headers.
AUTH-API-055.expected: The response has Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options or Content-Security-Policy, Referrer-Policy, and Cache-Control containing no-store.

AUTH-API-056.scenario: Verify that the login API does not allow a foreign website to call it from a browser
AUTH-API-056.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send an OPTIONS (pre-flight) request to /api/v1/auth/login with Origin https://evil.example.com, Access-Control-Request-Method POST and Access-Control-Request-Headers content-type.
Read the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header.
AUTH-API-056.expected: Access-Control-Allow-Origin is neither "*" nor "https://evil.example.com" - the foreign site is not allowed.

AUTH-API-057.scenario: Check that an authentication error carries a request ID for support tracing
AUTH-API-057.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with an unknown email, a password and a valid location.
Look for a request ID in the response body (requestId) or headers (X-Request-ID).
AUTH-API-057.expected: The error response includes a request ID (requestId in the body or an X-Request-ID header).

AUTH-API-060.scenario: Verify that repeated failed logins are throttled within 25 attempts
AUTH-API-060.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed. Opt-in test: runs only when RUN_LOCKOUT_TESTS=1 is set, because it can lock the account or throttle this machine's IP. Run it on its own at the end of a session.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/login with an unknown email, a wrong password and a valid location.
Read the response status.
Repeat the same request up to 25 times, stopping as soon as a 429 is returned.
AUTH-API-060.expected: The API starts answering 429 (Too Many Requests) within 25 failed attempts.

AUTH-API-061.scenario: Verify that repeated password-reset requests are throttled within 15 attempts
AUTH-API-061.preconditions: The API is reachable. No sign-in token is needed. Opt-in test: runs only when RUN_LOCKOUT_TESTS=1 is set, because it can lock the account or throttle this machine's IP. Run it on its own at the end of a session.
steps: Send a POST request to /api/v1/auth/forgot-password with a test email.
Read the response status.
Repeat the same request up to 15 times, stopping as soon as a 429 is returned.
AUTH-API-061.expected: The API starts answering 429 (Too Many Requests) within 15 requests, so the endpoint cannot be used to spam a mailbox.
